title: What You Wear
label: ch:ml-clothing
canDo: I can name what someone is wearing, and call it new or old.

payoff.summary: From cold: four things worn, two endings between them, and an adjective that has not moved since chapter 42.
payoff.note: Four atoms. THE EXAM POINT'S NOTE IS ACCURATE THIS TIME, and that was checked rather than assumed: the last two points worked (LEX-37, LEX-47) both had notes that overstated their gaps, so this one was token-swept first. thuni IS the only textile word taught (ML-C46-cloth), and not one garment is named -- shirt, mundu, sari, sandal, shoes, cap, glasses, watch, bag, dress and skirt all return ZERO occurrences. NO NEW GRAMMAR AT ALL, which is the point of the chapter after chapter 99 spent itself on three contrasting joins. Only two endings appear across the four words -- the half-u (mundu, cheruppu) and -i (saari, thoppi) -- and the learner owns both already -- and REVIEW CAUGHT THE PROVENANCE WRONG in the first draft, which said the half-u arrived with paattu and the ya with kali and bhangi. It did not: enthaaNu takes the half-u at sequence 130 and kuttiyaaNu takes the ya at 810, so those three are the most recent words to USE the joins, not the words they began with. Same defect chapter 98 recorded fixing when kali said 'two words now do this', returned in the same shape one chapter later. The frame is the attributive adjective from ML-C42: puthiya and pazhaya sit in front and do not change, which is that chapter's whole pattern applied to nouns it never had. THE GLYPH PRE-CHECK FAILED TWICE IN A NEW WAY AND WAS DEMOTED TO A SIGNAL. Its control had to be derived from the data rather than recalled, as in chapter 99 -- and then it produced FALSE NEGATIVES, refusing shirt for the chillu RR and 'to wear' for DHA, both of which appear in taught headwords already (ten and seven respectively). A check that is stricter than the rule it stands in for is not a gate; it is now used only to tell what needs a second look. shirt was dropped anyway, but on scope rather than on glyphs: mundu, saari, cheruppu and thoppi already cover all three limbs of the label -- clothing, footwear and accessories -- and a fifth clothing word adds no limb. EVERY ROMANIZATION WAS DERIVED LETTER BY LETTER rather than word by word -- the correction chapter 99 earned by getting nrttham's vowel right and the consonant beside it wrong. ca is c, witnessed by cintikkuka, cevi, cheRiya, chuNTu, cUlu, cEcci and cErkkuka among others, with chaaya, nenchu, uchakazhinju, acchan and muttacchan as legacy ch spellings; zha is zh-with-underdot, witnessed by pazhaya, pazham, vazhi and taazhe, against vyaazham, mazhakkaalam, ezhu and ML-S118's llla; NTu is witnessed exactly by chuNTu; and saari is witnessed inside samsaarikkuka's own romanization. puthiya and pazhaya were read off ML-C42's own fields rather than reconstructed. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS NOTE GAVE COUNTS INSTEAD OF NAMES -- 'sixteen headwords', 'the lone chaaya', 'six against two' -- and review found every one of them wrong (30 and 5; 12 and 6). They were offered as EVIDENCE OF the letter-by-letter discipline, in the same commit whose changelog says to name lessons and never count them. The rule existed and the sentence claiming rigour broke it.
